title: B1 Intermediate English Examination (CEFR / PET Standard)
description: Comprehensive CEFR B1 assessment evaluating Reading, Listening, Speaking, and Writing based on Cambridge Preliminary (PET) standards.

reading.instructions: Read the two passages carefully and answer questions r-q1 to r-q8. Pay attention to each question type (Multiple Choice, Multiple Select, Fill in the Blank, and True/False/Not Given).

passages.title: Passage 1: A Volunteer Vacation in Costa Rica
passages.content:
Last summer, twenty-year-old student Daniel decided to spend three weeks volunteering at a sea turtle conservation centre on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica. Instead of staying at a comfortable beach hotel with his friends, Daniel chose to live in a simple wooden cabin with four other international volunteers. Their daily routine was demanding but rewarding. Every night, the team walked along the sandy beach in shifts to search for nesting sea turtles and protect their eggs from wild animals and illegal collectors.

During the day, volunteers carried out different tasks around the camp. They cleaned the wooden hatcheries where eggs were kept safe until they hatched, repaired fences, and collected plastic waste washed ashore by ocean tides. Although the weather was hot and humid, and mosquitoes were a constant nuisance, Daniel found the work deeply satisfying. The highlight of his trip occurred in the second week, when over eighty baby turtles hatched early one morning. The volunteers gently carried them to the water's edge and watched them crawl safely into the ocean.

Daniel believes that the trip changed his attitude toward travel. 'In the past, I only wanted to relax on the beach or go shopping in big cities,' he explained. 'This trip showed me that travel can be meaningful. I learned how fragile ocean ecosystems are, and I made great friends from France, Japan, and Canada.' Daniel is already saving money to join another wildlife conservation project next year in South Africa.

questions.prompt: What was the main purpose of the night patrols on the beach?

options.text: To guide tourists safely back to their cabins
To find nesting turtles and keep their eggs safe from danger
To clean up plastic waste left behind by visitors
To catch wild animals that disturbed the camp

questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 specifies that every night the team walked in shifts to 'search for nesting sea turtles and protect their eggs from wild animals and illegal collectors'.

questions.prompt: Which TWO daytime responsibilities are mentioned in the second paragraph?

options.text: Cleaning the egg hatcheries
Cooking hot meals for other volunteers
Collecting plastic rubbish from the shore
Giving guided tours to hotel guests

questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that volunteers 'cleaned the wooden hatcheries' (A) and 'collected plastic waste washed ashore by ocean tides' (C).

questions.prompt: The most exciting moment of Daniel's volunteering experience happened during the ________ week of his stay.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 mentions: 'The highlight of his trip occurred in the second week, when over eighty baby turtles hatched...'

questions.prompt: Daniel has already reserved his flight tickets for his next volunteer trip to South Africa.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 notes that Daniel is saving money to join a project in South Africa, but it does not mention whether he has already booked or reserved flight tickets.

passages.title: Passage 2: Working from Home: The New Normal for Maria
passages.content:
Two years ago, Maria Garcia worked as a customer service representative in a busy office in central Manchester. Every morning, she spent more than an hour commuting by bus and train, often arriving at her desk already exhausted and stressed. When her employer decided to offer remote working options, Maria was initially worried that she would feel isolated from her colleagues. However, she quickly discovered that working from home offered significant advantages for her daily routine and overall well-being.

Today, Maria starts her day with a thirty-minute jog in the local park, followed by a healthy breakfast, before opening her laptop at eight-thirty. Without the daily commute, she saves nearly two hundred pounds every month on transportation costs and has more energy throughout the day. To stay organised, Maria set up a small workstation in the corner of her bedroom with an ergonomic chair and good lighting. She attends video meetings with her team every morning to review daily tasks, which helps her maintain strong professional connections.

Nevertheless, working remotely also presents some challenges. Maria admits that it can be difficult to separate work from leisure when living and working in the same environment. In the beginning, she frequently checked work emails late in the evening. To solve this problem, Maria created a strict rule: at five o'clock, she shuts down her computer and puts it inside a desk drawer until the next morning. She also schedules weekly coffee meetups with local friends to ensure she stays socially active outside work.

questions.prompt: What was Maria's main concern before she started working from home?

options.text: She feared she would spend too much money on home office equipment.
She was worried about feeling cut off and lonely without her colleagues.
She thought her internet connection would not be reliable enough.
She was afraid her working hours would be lengthened by her manager.

questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 notes that 'Maria was initially worried that she would feel isolated from her colleagues'.

questions.prompt: Which TWO positive outcomes of remote working for Maria are highlighted in the second paragraph?

options.text: Saving money each month on travel expenses
Receiving a salary increase from her company
Having higher energy levels throughout the day
Having a whole spare room dedicated exclusively to office work

questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that she 'saves nearly two hundred pounds every month on transportation costs' (A) and 'has more energy throughout the day' (C). (Option D is incorrect because her workspace is in a corner of her bedroom).

questions.prompt: To stop working late at night, Maria follows a rule to turn off her computer at ________ o'clock every day.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 states: '...at five o'clock, she shuts down her computer and puts it inside a desk drawer until the next morning.'

questions.prompt: Maria's home office workstation is located in a dedicated private study room.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that Maria 'set up a small workstation in the corner of her bedroom', not in a separate private study room.

listening.instructions: Listen to the recordings or read the transcripts carefully, then answer questions l-q1 to l-q6.

parts.title: Part 1: Planning a Weekend Trip to York

audioConfig.overallStyle: casual friendly exchange, clear enunciation for B1 exam

parts.transcript:
Sam: Hi, Chloe! Did you get a chance to look at train tickets for our weekend trip to York next Saturday?
Chloe: Yes, I checked online this morning. If we catch the early train at seven in the morning, a return ticket is only twenty-five pounds each. But if we take the train at nine, the price doubles to fifty pounds!
Sam: Wow, that's a huge difference. I don't mind waking up early if it saves us twenty-five pounds. What about accommodation?
Chloe: My cousin recommended a small guest house near the city centre called Green Gardens. It's clean, reasonably priced, and hot breakfast is included. However, we should book today because they only have two double rooms left.
Sam: That sounds great. Let's purchase the seven o'clock train tickets right now, and you can reserve the room this afternoon.

questions.prompt: Why do Sam and Chloe decide to take the 7:00 AM train instead of the 9:00 AM train?

options.text: The nine o'clock train was already sold out.
The early ticket is twenty-five pounds cheaper per person.
They want to arrive in time for breakfast at the guest house.
Chloe's cousin is meeting them at the station at eight o'clock.

questions.explanation: Chloe explains that the 7:00 AM return ticket costs twenty-five pounds, while the 9:00 AM train costs fifty pounds. Sam agrees to wake up early to save twenty-five pounds.

questions.prompt: The name of the guest house recommended by Chloe's cousin is ________.
questions.explanation: Chloe mentions: 'My cousin recommended a small guest house near the city centre called Green Gardens.'

parts.title: Part 2: Radio Interview with a Young Bakery Owner

audioConfig.overallStyle: professional local radio interview, polite and articulate

parts.transcript:
Interviewer: Welcome back to Our Local Community. Today, I'm speaking with Liam Evans, who opened 'The Daily Crust' bakery six months ago in town. Liam, how did your passion for baking begin?
Liam: Well, I actually studied graphic design at university and worked in an office for two years. But sitting at a desk all day wasn't for me. My grandfather was a professional baker, and when I was a teenager, he taught me traditional bread-making techniques every Sunday. That's where my love for it started.
Interviewer: Starting a new business can be tough. What has been the biggest challenge so far?
Liam: Definitely the working hours! We start preparing the dough at three-thirty every morning so our bread and pastries are fresh when we open at seven. Getting used to waking up so early was very hard at first, but seeing our happy regular customers makes it completely worthwhile.

questions.prompt: Who taught Liam how to make bread when he was younger?

options.text: His university design professor
His former office manager
His grandfather
A baker at a local supermarket

questions.explanation: Liam explains: 'My grandfather was a professional baker, and when I was a teenager, he taught me traditional bread-making techniques...'

questions.prompt: Liam completed a degree in business management before opening his bakery.
questions.explanation: Liam states that he 'studied graphic design at university', not business management.

parts.title: Part 3: Sports Centre Student Orientation

audioConfig.overallStyle: clear university orientation announcement, authoritative and welcoming

speakers.name: Coordinator
speakers.style: authoritative, clear enunciation for student orientation

parts.transcript: Coordinator: Good afternoon, students, and welcome to the university sports centre orientation. Whether you want to play competitive badminton or just keep fit, we have more than twelve clubs you can join this term. To participate, you must register through the student website before this Friday at six in the evening. The term membership costs thirty pounds, which gives you full access to both the gym and the swimming pool. Please remember that all members must bring clean indoor sports shoes and their own water bottle to every session. You can borrow a locker key from reception by leaving your student ID card while you exercise.

questions.prompt: Which TWO items are students required to bring with them to each sports session?

options.text: Clean indoor sports shoes
Their own padlock for the lockers
A personal water bottle
A printed receipt of membership

questions.explanation: The coordinator specifies: '...all members must bring clean indoor sports shoes (A) and their own water bottle (C) to every session.'

questions.prompt: In order to borrow a locker key at the reception desk, students must leave their ________.
questions.explanation: The coordinator announces: 'You can borrow a locker key from reception by leaving your student ID card while you exercise.'

speaking.instructions: Read the prompts below and prepare your spoken response. You should speak clearly for about 1 to 2 minutes on each topic.

tasks.title: Part 1: Describing a Favourite Free-Time Activity
tasks.prompt:
Describe a hobby or free-time activity that you really enjoy.
You should say:
- What the activity is
- Where and when you usually do it
- Who you do it with
And explain why this activity is important or enjoyable to you.

rubric.description: Speaks at a steady pace with clear ideas linked by basic connectors (e.g., 'because', 'although', 'so', 'after that').
Uses everyday vocabulary accurately to describe habits, feelings, and personal preferences.
Accurate use of present simple, past simple, and basic modal verbs with reasonable grammatical control.

tasks.sampleAnswer: One of my favourite free-time activities is cycling. I usually go cycling on Saturday mornings in a large park near my house, where there are special paths surrounded by trees and a lake. I often cycle with my older brother, but sometimes I go alone if I want to listen to music or a podcast. I really enjoy cycling because it helps me stay healthy and energetic after a busy week of studying. It also gives me a chance to spend time outdoors in nature, which helps me feel relaxed and clears my mind.

tasks.title: Part 2: A Skill You Would Like to Learn
tasks.prompt:
Talk about a new skill or subject you would like to learn in the future.
You should say:
- What skill or subject it is
- How you plan to learn it
- How long you think it will take
And explain why you think this skill will be useful for you.

rubric.description: Expresses thoughts clearly and logically using future forms and simple explanations.
Demonstrates appropriate everyday vocabulary related to learning, technology, and personal goals.
Good control of future expressions ('would like to', 'am planning to', 'will') and conditional sentences ('if I practice...').

tasks.sampleAnswer: In the future, I would really like to learn how to edit videos using computer software. I plan to take an online course on the weekend and watch video tutorials on YouTube. I think it will take about three or four months of regular practice to learn the basic tools and effects. This skill will be very useful for me because I want to create short travel videos for my family and friends. Furthermore, many companies now look for people with digital media skills, so it might also help me find a good job after I finish university.

writing.instructions: Complete both writing tasks. Make sure you meet the minimum word count and address all points in the prompts.

tasks.title: Task 1: Informal Email to a Friend
tasks.prompt:
An English friend named Alex is planning to visit your hometown next month. Read this extract from Alex's email:

'I am coming to visit your city for three days next month! Can you suggest some interesting places for us to visit? What kind of weather should I expect, and what clothes do you recommend I pack?'

Write an email replying to Alex. Answer all of Alex's questions.

rubric.description: Answers all parts of the prompt: recommends places to visit, explains the weather, and suggests clothes to pack.
Uses an appropriate informal, friendly tone suitable for an email to a friend.
Logically structured with clear greetings, paragraph breaks, and basic linking words.
Demonstrates good control of B1 vocabulary and simple to compound sentence structures with minimal errors.

tasks.sampleAnswer:
Hi Alex,

It is wonderful to hear from you! I am so excited that you are visiting my city next month.

There are many great things to see here. First, we should visit the historic castle in the city centre because the views from the top are fantastic. We can also explore the lively riverside market, where you can try delicious traditional snacks and buy souvenirs.

Next month is usually mild during the day, but it can get quite chilly and windy in the evening. It also rains from time to time, so you should pack a warm jacket, comfortable walking shoes, and an umbrella.

Let me know your flight details when you book them. I can't wait to see you!

Best wishes,
Sam

tasks.title: Task 2: Short Article for a School Website
tasks.prompt:
You see this announcement on an international student website:

'Articles Wanted!
How Digital Technology Helps Me Learn
Do you use mobile apps, websites, or digital devices for your studies? Tell us which digital tools you use, how they help your learning, and whether you still like using traditional paper books.'

Write an article answering these questions.

rubric.description: Covers all three points: tools used, benefits to learning, and personal view on traditional books.
Has a clear title, introduction, body paragraphs, and a brief conclusion.
Employs a range of vocabulary related to study, technology, and personal opinion.
Correct use of present simple, comparison structures ('easier than', 'more convenient'), and modal verbs.

tasks.sampleAnswer:
How Digital Technology Helps Me Learn

Digital technology plays an important role in my daily studies. I regularly use my tablet and smartphone to prepare for classes and practise foreign languages.

One tool I use every day is a language learning app called Duolingo. It allows me to practise English vocabulary and grammar for fifteen minutes whenever I am on the bus. In addition, I often watch educational videos on YouTube, which explain difficult science topics with helpful animations and simple diagrams.

However, although digital tools are fast and convenient, I still enjoy reading traditional printed books. In my opinion, reading from paper is much easier on the eyes, especially when I need to study for several hours before an exam. In conclusion, combining modern technology with traditional books provides the best learning experience for students today.
